newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Limited production at strike hit Mondi mill.
newsitem.headline: Limited production at strike hit Mondi mill.

text.p: Limited production is continuing at the paper division of Mondi, a subsidiary of Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd, after a legal wage strike by workers on Wednesday, a mill manager said on Friday.
Two of the mill's five paper machines were in operation and management expected to start up a third machine by Friday afternoon, Peter Lynch said in a statement.

The Merebank mill near Durban, which produces up to 500,000 tonnes of publication, business and education papers annually, had strong stockholdings and no major difficulties could be foreseen in supplying customers, he said.
He said the 642 striking workers formed part of a 1,324 strong workforce at the mill and were demanding an increase in excess of 11 percent across the board. Mondi Paper has offered 9.5 percent.

The Paper, Printing, Wood and Allied Workers' Union representing the workers has threatened to call workers allied to the union in other Mondi divisions out on strike to strengthen their bargaining position.

"We are calling a meeting on Monday for shop stewards from all Mondi's divisions if the strike is not settled by then. They have said they are ready to support us," spokesman Mhlaba Mkhize told Reuters.
He said negotiations had stalled between the union and management but "we are ready when they are".
Lynch said the dispute had been referred to the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration but the process had not resolved the deadlock.
